title: Scope each train to one coherent journey

facts.note: Train spec files are identifiable by their kind/location in the plan.
Fires when a train spec is authored, edited, or reviewed (including review of an unchanged existing train).
Planning or review task mentions defining, resizing, or checking a train.

values: wagon flow kind or feedback loop changed
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer comparing the train's wagons, outcome, flow kinds, feedback loops and participant themes before and after; a wagon-internal edit can affect journey coherence through these.
Wagon count is mechanically countable; the one-journey test and whether a decomposition signal really indicates multiple journeys require judgment.

fires: Planner authors a new train listing its wagons and outcome.
Planner adds wagons to an existing train, pushing it to 8 or more.
Planner or reviewer reviews an existing, unchanged train for scope.
A train's outcome sentence needs 'and' to describe what it delivers.
A train has only one wagon.
A wagon edit introduces an exploratory (gesture) flow into a core-mechanic train, adds an independent feedback loop, or adds participants from another theme.
doesNotFire: Editing a single wagon's internals (e.g. wording of WMBTs or acceptances) in a way that changes neither train membership, outcome, flow kind, feedback loops, nor participant themes.
Code changes in implementation layers that do not touch or review train specs.

given: A plan contains a train and its wagons, being authored, edited, or reviewed (including an unchanged existing train or a wagon change that may alter the train's journey).
when: The planner sets or checks the train's outcome and which wagons it contains.
then: The train must tell ONE coherent journey: if its outcome cannot be stated in one sentence without 'and', split it.
prefer: Size: 3-7 wagons is the recommended sweet spot; 2 is the allowed minimum.
At 8-12 wagons, review whether the train holds multiple journeys (split if it does); at 13+, decompose.

Treat these as decomposition signals to investigate (do they mean multiple journeys?): outcome with multiple 'AND's; both setup AND teardown of a lifecycle; mix of exploratory (gesture) and core-mechanic flows; multiple independent feedback loops; participants from 3+ themes.
avoid: Trains of 13+ wagons (antipattern), e.g. a 16-wagon 'complete lifecycle' train spanning multiple journeys.
why: A train demonstrates one user journey end to end; bundling journeys hides independent outcomes and makes the train too large to review and accept as one story.
evidence: Reviewer states the train outcome in one sentence without 'and' (one_journey_test).
Wagon count: 3-7 recommended, 2 minimum, 8-12 flagged for review (multiple journeys?), 13+ decompose, 1 below minimum.
Reviewer checks the train for decomposition_signal entries; each present signal indicates the train may be multiple journeys.
verifier_detail: Size bands by wagon count: <2 = below minimum; 2 = minimum allowed; 3-7 = recommended (sweet spot); 8-12 = warning ('multiple journeys?'); 13+ = antipattern (decompose).
one_journey_test: can the outcome be stated in ONE sentence without 'and'? If not, split.

decomposition_signal (signals a train is multiple journeys): outcome description contains multiple 'AND' conjunctions; train has both setup AND teardown (match lifecycle); mix of exploratory (gesture) AND core mechanic flows; multiple independent feedback loops; participants from 3+ different themes.
Calibration examples: good = train:decision:standard (5 wagons, one outcome); bad = train:match:solo-match-complete (16 wagons, multiple journeys).
